thread:
ravi: Heads up — I’m seeing a spike of fncall schema rejects getting routed to the degen path in eu-west. Dashboard cost metric shows a +12% token bump in the last 10m :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: Yikes. Do we have the validator_error_type in the events? Need to know if these are missing required fields vs wrong types.

jamie: console-bot just posted an alert earlier: "schema-validator alert: type=missing_field count=42 route=degen". That’s what's showing up in the ops feed.

ravi: Yeah, log snippet from the api nodes: 
```
WARN validate_fncall: req_id=abc123 validator_error=missing_field
  field=tool.args.user_id route_suggest=degen
```

alex: Two separate problems: routing policy sends malformed outputs to degen (expected), but we still bill/attribute those tokens and they show up in the model-cost dashboard without clear rejection tags. UX wise console shows increased spend but not what caused it.

maria: We should add a telemetry dimension: validation_outcome = {accepted, soft_reject, hard_reject} and validation_reason enum. Then dashboards can facet costs by these.

jamie: Agreed. Also need to decide whether soft_rejects should be counted as normal requests for billing or as operational noise. Customer-impacting rejects should definitely be billed; parser noise maybe not.

ravi: For rollouts, the strict-validate can be toggled per-canary slice. We need dashboard visibility per-slice otherwise we’ll miss correlation between enabling strict and quota events.

alex: Proposal: add route_id + validator_reason to all metrics (prom labels) and to the trace/span tags. Example metric: fncall_requests_total{route="degen",validator_reason="missing_field",outcome="hard_reject"}++

maria: +1 but careful about label cardinality. validator_reason is small enum (missing_field, wrong_type, extra_props, parse_error). route_id is already limited. Should be fine.

jamie: Also frontend change: in the per-model page, create a panel "Validation rejects" that shows a sparkline and top reasons with links to sample requests (redact PII). So SRE and product can triage.

ravi: Who owns the console work? Product or infra? We need a quick probe tile first, not a full panel.

alex: Platform can wire up the metric + tags. Product can add UI tile next sprint. infra to own backend sampling API for redacted request samples.

maria: Sampling — we should surface a sample rate per validator_reason and per-route for the UI. e.g., sample=0.1 for noise reasons, sample=1.0 for failures above threshold.

jamie: On the billing side: add a flag in billing pipeline that marks requests with outcome=hard_reject to a separate billing bucket. Legal/product can decide if we charge. For now, tag them but don't change billing.

console-bot: alert: schema-validator: type=missing_field count=47 route=degen sampling=0.1

alex: One operational edge: when strict-validate is enabled during canary we sometimes route to fallback model variant which still consumes tokens. We should show fallback_model in traces so owners know which variant took traffic.

maria: Good call. Add fallback_model label and route_then_variant to traces.

ravi: Can platform team produce a short RFC with metric names, label enums, and a small rollout plan? I can run a quick canary after implementation.

jamie: I’ll draft the RFC. Quick checklist I’ll include:
- metric names + Prom examples
- validator_reason enum defs
- sampling knobs + default rates
- console probe wireframe + link to samples API
- billing tagging behavior (tag only)

alex: Also add an alerting rule: if hard_rejects_rate per-route > 1% sustained for 5m AND token_spike > 10% then page oncall with a clear message.

maria: UX note: show a tooltip on the dashboard explaining what a degen route means and why requests are routed there — product asks users get fewer surprises.

ravi: Sounds good. Jamie — can you post RFC link here when ready? I’ll block time for validation in the canary window tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

jamie: Will do. Putting an initial stub in docs: https://console.redwood.ai/rfcs/validator-metrics-stub (WIP)

console-bot: deploy-bot: deployment queued by jamie for feature/validator-metrics (staging).

alex: Nice. After staging run, capture a 30m trace with both accepted and rejected flows and attach to RFC. That will help product decide billing treatment.

maria: One final ask: ensure samples API redacts any field named email, phone, token, or ssn by default.

ravi: Agreed. Thanks all — followups in RFC channel. :thumbsup:
